title: AP Campaign-Promise Tracker Does Not Identify the Pledge in This Record
description_short: AP Campaign-Promise Tracker Does Not Identify the Pledge in This Record
description_medium: The AP tracker organizes Trump’s campaign promises by reported progress and can be revisited as outcomes change. The supplied record does not name the pledge, the relevant tracker row, or the review dates behind its claim of repeated cycles. Without that information, the asserted long-term credibility risk cannot be tied to a specific outcome.
notes: The linked AP page confirms a promise-tracking project but does not identify the pledge, dated status changes, or review cycles behind this entry. Provide the specific pledge and dated tracker results before asserting a long-tail credibility effect.

title: Trump Order Directs Agencies to Review Rules and Enforcement Priorities
description_short: Trump Order Directs Agencies to Review Rules and Enforcement Priorities
description_medium: Trump’s Feb. 19, 2025 deregulatory order directed agencies to identify rules the administration viewed as legally questionable or burdensome and to review enforcement priorities. A July 2025 report documented OSHA proposals to revise or withdraw more than two dozen rules, most still open to comment. The record shows a review and proposed changes—not the elimination of federal rule-making.
description_long: On Feb. 19, 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order directing agencies to identify regulations the administration considered legally questionable, costly, or inconsistent with its priorities. Skadden’s analysis says agencies were asked to provide inventories to the Office of Management and Budget and to reconsider enforcement of certain rules; it describes a process likely to generate rule changes and litigation, not a completed dismantling of every regulator. A separate July 2025 account documented more than two dozen proposed Occupational Safety and Health Administration rules. The proposals included revising the agency’s interpretation of workplace hazards and withdrawing or modifying several standards. Most were still in a public-comment period, so they had not taken effect as final rules. The sources show a broad deregulatory agenda and concrete proposals, while also distinguishing proposals from rules already changed. They do not support claims that the EPA, FDA, FTC, SEC, and OSHA had all lost rule-making powers, that thousands of experts were replaced by lobbyists, or that decades of protections were eliminated. Those sweeping assertions have been removed from this entry.
notes: Replaced unsupported claims of complete multi-agency destruction with actions and proposals documented by the linked sources; OSHA proposals were not yet final.

title: Trump Played Trophy Host While His War Team Sat in the Situation Room
description_short: Trump Played Trophy Host While His War Team Sat in the Situation Room
description_medium: At a March 20, 2026 ceremony, Trump presented the Commander-in-Chief’s Trophy to Navy after its 2025 win over Army. He said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chair Dan Caine were in the White House Situation Room as the Iran conflict continued. The AP report records Trump’s remarks and the ceremony; it does not assess the military operation.
description_long: On March 20, 2026, President Donald Trump presented the Commander-in-Chief’s Trophy to the Navy football team, which had beaten Army in the 2025 game. During the ceremony, he referred to the continuing Iran conflict and said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, were in the White House Situation Room. Trump offered no operational details, saying only that the United States was “doing extremely well.” The Associated Press also reported that an official said three additional warships and roughly 2,500 Marines were being sent to the Middle East. The report documents a public ceremony taking place while senior officials handled war-related work elsewhere in the White House. It does not establish that the trophy event affected military decisions, that Trump was absent from crisis management, or that the ceremony was intended to turn the conflict into a spectacle. The entry is about the juxtaposition in Trump’s public remarks and the reported deployment, not a judgment on the military operation’s conduct or outcome.

preserved_fields.title: Trump Played Trophy Host While His War Team Sat in the Situation Room
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump Played Trophy Host While His War Team Sat in the Situation Room

notes: Changed the noncanonical category to Foreign Policy and replaced editorial claims with the facts reported by the AP.

title: Guardian Reports on Peale’s Anti-Catholic Politics and Trump’s Criticism of Pope Leo
description_short: Guardian Reports on Peale’s Anti-Catholic Politics and Trump’s Criticism of Pope Leo
description_medium: The Guardian placed Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo alongside the history of Norman Vincent Peale, the pastor at the Manhattan church Trump attended as a teenager and the officiant at his first wedding. When Trump was 14, Peale led Protestant clergy who opposed John F. Kennedy’s candidacy because Kennedy was Catholic. The report offers historical context, not proof of motive.
description_long: The Guardian’s April 18, 2026 report examined whether Donald Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo might have roots in his early religious background. Trump attended Manhattan’s Marble Collegiate Church as a teenager, where Norman Vincent Peale was pastor; Peale later officiated at Trump’s first wedding. When Trump was 14, Peale led a group of Protestant clergy who publicly opposed John F. Kennedy’s presidential candidacy because Kennedy was Catholic. The Guardian connects that history to Trump’s criticism of Pope Leo after the pope objected to the U.S. attack on Iran. The article supplies a historical parallel and quotes the anti-Catholic argument Peale’s group advanced, including fears that a Catholic president would be controlled by the pope. It does not establish that Peale’s views caused Trump’s position, that Trump shares those views, or that a childhood grievance explains the current dispute. The original title’s psychological framing goes beyond what the report demonstrates. This entry describes the reported history and the present disagreement while keeping the proposed connection explicitly speculative.

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Pope Obsession Looked Like a Very Old Grievance in Religious Drag
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Pope Obsession Looked Like a Very Old Grievance in Religious Drag
preserved_fields.description_medium: Manhattan church led by Norman Vincent Peale was known for opposing presidency of JFK – and Catholics in general. It fit the larger pattern of Trump treating spiritual language, religious authority, and public morality as arenas for grievance, ego, and old resentments rather than humility or reflection.

notes: Retitled to remove a psychological claim the Guardian presents only as a possibility; the source does not establish a causal link.

title: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation
description_short: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation
description_medium: PEN America’s 2024 analysis said Project 2025 proposed either eliminating the U.S. Agency for Global Media or weakening the editorial independence of its outlets, including Voice of America. It also described proposals affecting Radio Free Asia and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. These sources document a policy proposal and advocacy concerns, but do not verify the later closure or transformation asserted by this entry.
description_long: PEN America’s October 2024 analysis describes Project 2025 as a policy proposal, not a record of actions already taken by a later administration. It says the plan called for either eliminating the U.S. Agency for Global Media or changing its outlets’ editorial structure, and identifies Voice of America, Radio Free Asia, and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty among the services affected. The report also discusses proposals to alter the Open Technology Fund and public-broadcasting support. PEN argues that removing editorial independence could turn publicly supported outlets into partisan instruments; that is the organization’s assessment of the proposal’s likely consequences. The linked materials support describing the plan and the warning from press-freedom advocates. They do not establish that USAGM was eliminated, that VOA stopped operating, which employees or broadcasts were affected, or that the outlets were converted into propaganda services during the period named in this record. A dated government action or contemporaneous reporting on implementation is needed before those claims can be presented as completed events.

preserved_fields.title: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation
preserved_fields.description_short: Voice of America and USAGM Media Closure - International Broadcasting Propaganda Transformation

notes: The linked reports substantiate the Project 2025 proposal and PEN America’s analysis, but not the actual closure or transformation claimed by the title. A dated implementation source is needed.

title: Carl Icahn Takes TWA Private, Adding Debt Before Its 1995 Bankruptcy
description_short: Carl Icahn Takes TWA Private, Adding Debt Before Its 1995 Bankruptcy
description_medium: Carl Icahn took control of Trans World Airlines in 1985 and took it private in 1988. A linked account says Icahn received $469 million in the deal while TWA took on $540 million in debt. He left the company in 1993; TWA entered bankruptcy in 1995. The source links Icahn to Trump but does not attribute TWA’s financial decisions to Trump.
description_long: Carl Icahn became the owner of Trans World Airlines in 1985, when the airline was an important St. Louis employer. The linked TrumpFile account says he took TWA private in 1988, receiving $469 million while the airline assumed $540 million in debt. It quotes a former TWA executive saying Icahn appeared more interested in using the airline as a financial vehicle than in growing it. Icahn left the company in 1993, and TWA filed for bankruptcy two years later. These details describe the sequence and the reported financing, but they do not by themselves establish that Icahn’s decisions alone caused TWA’s collapse or the later economic trajectory of St. Louis. The account also notes a longstanding relationship between Icahn and Donald Trump and Icahn’s service as a Trump administration adviser in 2017. That association is context only: the 1980s TWA transaction preceded the advisory role and is not presented as an action by Trump.
notes: Retitled to focus on the documented TWA transaction; the source does not attribute the airline’s restructuring to Trump or prove that Icahn alone caused its later bankruptcy.

title: Donald Trump retaliates against WSJ reporter for negative press
description_short: Donald Trump retaliates against WSJ reporter for negative press
description_medium: In April 1991, Donald Trump offered Wall Street Journal reporter Neil Barsky and his family tickets to a boxing match, valued by the linked timeline at $3,000. After Barsky published another critical report on Trump’s finances, a Trump spokesman accused him of extortion in a conversation later reported by the New York Post. Barsky was moved off the Trump beat in June.
description_long: The linked timeline places the incident in April 1991, when Donald Trump offered Wall Street Journal reporter Neil Barsky and his family tickets to the Evander Holyfield–George Foreman boxing match in Atlantic City. It valued the tickets at $3,000 and says Barsky wanted to decline them, although his editor encouraged him to accept. Weeks later, Barsky published another critical story about Trump’s finances. The timeline reports that a Trump spokesman then called a New York Post contact and accused Barsky of extorting Trump by seeking tickets and other favors in exchange for favorable coverage. The Post published the allegation. Barsky continued reporting on Trump’s financial troubles and was moved to a different beat in June. This chronology raises questions about gifts to a reporter and the response to his coverage, but the linked page does not establish that the ticket offer was a bribe or that Trump personally ordered Barsky’s reassignment. Those distinctions matter: the reported sequence is documented by the timeline, while motive and causation remain claims or interpretation.

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump retaliates against WSJ reporter for negative press
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump retaliates against WSJ reporter for negative press

notes: Descriptions retain the reported chronology and attribute the allegation to the timeline; they do not state that a bribe or retaliatory order was proven.

title: The New York Times Releases a Flattering Profile of Jeffrey Epstein, According to TrumpFile
description_short: The New York Times Releases a Flattering Profile of Jeffrey Epstein, According to TrumpFile
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline entry dated Jan. 3, 2008 says The New York Times published a favorable profile of Jeffrey Epstein arranged by publicist Howard Rubenstein. It notes that Rubenstein also represented the Trump and Kushner families, but provides no link to the original Times article or evidence that Trump participated in or influenced its publication.
notes: The linked TrumpFile page offers a characterization of a 2008 Times profile and names its publicist, but supplies no original article link, title, author, or text. It does not document Trump’s involvement. The original article or contemporaneous reporting is needed to support a fuller description.
The original category was not in the repository’s canonical list; Press Freedom best fits the media-publication event described by the source.
